title: BCCI Holds High-Level Review as Rohit Sharma's ODI Future Faces Scrutiny
excerpt: India's cricket board convened captains Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer alongside head coach Gautam Gambhir at its Mumbai headquarters to dissect recent series losses and chart a roadmap to the 2027 ODI World Cup.
body:
• The BCCI held a long-awaited review meeting on September 3 at its Mumbai headquarters, with captains Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer, head coach Gautam Gambhir, and CoE director VVS Laxman in attendance.
  • BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia dismissed speculation about Rohit Sharma's ODI future, calling his recent form "superb" and confirming no changes to the coaching staff or selection committee.
  • Chief selector Ajit Agarkar was absent due to short notice and connectivity issues, drawing attention despite the board's insistence the meeting was routine.
  • The discussion focused on India's series losses in England and Ireland, injury management for key players, and strategic planning for the 2027 ODI World Cup in Southern Africa.

The Board of Control for Cricket in India convened a much-delayed review meeting at its Mumbai headquarters on September 3, bringing together the men's team's top decision-makers to examine a stretch of overseas results that has tested both patience and planning.

India's Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, head coach Gautam Gambhir, and Centre of Excellence director VVS Laxman all attended in person. They were joined by BCCI President Mithun Manhas, Secretary Devajit Saikia, Joint Secretary Prabhtej Singh Bhatia, and interim CEO Hemang Amin.

Rohit Sharma's Position Secure

The meeting was shadowed by speculation about veteran opener Rohit Sharma's role in the ODI setup ahead of the 2027 World Cup in Southern Africa. Saikia moved quickly to quash those questions.

"He is playing superbly in all matches. So, what more do you want? In the last match, he scored 138–148 runs. So why is there speculation? I do not want to give fodder to the speculators."

— Devajit Saikia, BCCI Secretary

Rohit, who stepped down from the T20I captaincy after the 2026 T20 World Cup triumph, continues to hold his place in the ODI side under captain Gill. The futures of Virat Kohli and Ravindra Jadeja in the 50-over format were also reportedly on the agenda, though both are understood to hold firm positions for now.

Dissecting the Overseas Struggles

Originally planned for July to address India's dismal T20I series defeats — a 2-0 loss in Ireland and a 4-0 whitewash in England — the meeting was postponed through the Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka tours. India recovered form in those assignments, winning the T20I series against Zimbabwe 3-0 and taking the Test series in Sri Lanka 1-0, providing some counterbalance to the earlier disappointments.

The review took a broader scope, evaluating performances across all four recent tours. The ODI series loss in England, where Gill's side went down 2-1, added to concerns. A 125-run collapse at Nottingham was flagged as a low point, according to SportsTak.

Saikia said the board had engaged in "soul-searching" about what went wrong and developed strategies for future tours of SENA (South Africa, England, New Zealand, Australia) countries.

Injury Crisis and Agarkar's Absence

Player fitness emerged as a central concern. Jasprit Bumrah missed the Sri Lanka series with a knee flare-up. Hardik Pandya, viewed as critical to the World Cup campaign, has been sidelined with a shin injury, and his workload capacity as a seam-bowling all-rounder remains uncertain.

Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy, and Harshit Rana are provisionally selected for the upcoming Afghanistan T20I series in Delhi from September 13–17 but face fitness evaluations at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru on September 9.

Chief selector Ajit Agarkar's absence drew attention. Saikia explained that the meeting was called at short notice and Agarkar was out of Mumbai, unable to connect even remotely. The BCCI secretary denied reports that Agarkar's tenure was under review or that a director of cricket would be appointed.

What's Next

Looking ahead, India faces a packed schedule: the Afghanistan T20I series in September, a multi-format tour of New Zealand in November, and the Border-Gavaskar Trophy at home before the World Cup. The board is pushing for better coordination between medical staff, conditioning teams, and selectors to manage workloads across formats.

"We have basically discussed our way forward regarding team preparations because we have a busy schedule ahead," Saikia said. "When the selectors meet to pick the team for the West Indies series and thereafter for the New Zealand series, they will consider whatever parameters they deem necessary."

No team selections were made at the meeting, and no changes to the support staff were discussed. The BCCI's stated priority remains a strong showing at the 2027 ODI World Cup — and everything between now and then will be evaluated against that target.
image_caption: Rohit Sharma, the Indian cricket captain, faces questions about his ODI future following a high-level BCCI review.
